explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is a project-specific step in building Leray solutions. It works with the library's own objects (`Vec3`, `ParabolicPoint`, `L2Vec3`, `vec3EuclideanNorm`) and with sequences of time-slice fields. It combines a uniform energy bound, weak convergence on compact sets and lower semicontinuity of slices to get weak L² convergence of the pairings at every positive time. The proof's main step is the library's own lemma `lerayLimit_globalSlices_of_localWeak`. The Mathlib lemmas it uses are routine tools: `aecover_closedBall`, `setLIntegral_le_lintegral`, `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero` and `MemLp.continuousLinearMap_comp`. None of these carries the theorem's content. I did not run a search because the statement is so tied to the library's definitions. Mathlib has no ready-made result of this form (going from local weak L² convergence plus a uniform bound to global weak convergence for these particular vector fields), and a derivation would need a real argument, not one or two lines.
